_why: EVERY PERSON'S URL, FROZEN. Written once per person and never recomputed.
build_people.py's scheme is better than most in the estate: it
disambiguates namesakes by HOUSEHOLD, which is data, rather than by
position. It still moves. `base if counts[base] == 1` flips a person from
`maria-porrino` to `maria-porrino-of-...` the moment a SECOND Maria
Porrino is read, and the `+= "-2"` fallback is pure iteration order.
Seventeen URLs moved between 61cf9ae and f6cc705 — maria-porrino,
matteo-carfora, nicola-crisci among them.
THE KEY IS THE ONE build_people.py ALREADY USES. For a register person it
is the frozen household id plus the person string — `key = h["id"] + "|"
+ m["person"]`, which this archive minted on 23 September when it stopped
keying households on their display name. For a tree-only person it is
`tree:<treeId>`. Thirty-four slugs are claimed by two keys, which is
correct: those are people the register and the tree both hold, and both
keys must lead to the same page.
A slug is never edited and never deleted, including for somebody removed
from the tree, because a published URL is a promise and the address must
not pass to a different person.
Seeded 23 September 2026 from the slugs the site was already serving.
The position is the Defranceski archive's, of the same day: a page is a
person, an id is frozen, a name is an index.
